behavior: An explicit serve-signed entrypoint requires an absolute executable, exact SHA256 pin, namespace and reader/writer role.
Only the selected mode receives signed-v1 policy fields. Ordinary serve and CI startup retain their existing mode.
Storage credentials and bearer enter the backend only through its explicit environment. Artifact signing keys and unrelated parent environment are excluded.
The executable and pin come from independent owner approval; matching a supplied pin is not approval or proof of server policy support.

limits: The process boundary test does not establish native signature verification, strict server policy semantics or actual R2 capabilities.
Resource envelopes and PID/listener ownership belong to the still-pending parent supervisor; this exec mode does not claim them.
Current normal-source stable/canary qualification, immutable protected publication, rollout, rotation/rollback and real observation windows remain required.
reversal: Stop using the opt-in entrypoint and revert this additive source change. Existing services continue invoking ordinary serve; no live service or cloud setting is changed by this component.
